state_tax.work_common_tail: . Exemption-credit rules (Form 540): Line 7 (personal): Form 540 line 7 "Personal: If you checked box 1, 3, or 4 above, enter 1 in the box. If you checked box 2 or 5, enter 2 in the box. If you checked the box on line 6, see instructions." (the filing-status boxes: 1 Single, 2 Married/RDP filing jointly, 3 Married/RDP filing separately, 4 Head of household, 5 Qualifying surviving spouse/RDP). Booklet p. 12, Line 6: "Check the box on line 6 if someone else can claim you or your spouse/RDP as a dependent on their tax return, even if they chose not to." Line 7, when line 6 is checked: "Single or married/RDP filing separately, enter -0-." "Head of household, enter -0-." "Married/RDP filing jointly and both you and your spouse/RDP can be claimed as dependents, enter -0-." "Married/RDP filing jointly and only one spouse/RDP can be claimed as a dependent, enter 1." Line 8 (blind): Form 540 line 8 "Blind: If you (or your spouse/RDP) are visually impaired, enter 1; if both are visually impaired, enter 2." Booklet p. 12, Line 8: "Visually impaired means not capable of seeing better than 20/200 while wearing glasses or contact lenses, or if your field of vision is not more than 20 degrees." "The first year you claim this exemption credit, attach a doctor's statement to the back of Form 540 indicating you or your spouse/RDP are visually impaired." "Do not claim this credit if someone else can claim you as a dependent on their tax return." Only a joint return enters 2: the second count is the spouse/RDP's ("if both"). A single or head-of-household return has no spouse/RDP on it, and a separate return counts the filer alone (booklet p. 5, "Married/RDP Filing Separately": "You cannot claim a personal exemption credit for your spouse/RDP even if your spouse/RDP had no income, is not filing a tax return, and is not claimed as a dependent on another person's tax return."). On a qualifying surviving spouse/RDP return the spouse/RDP died in an earlier year (p. 5: "Your spouse/RDP died in 2023 or 2024 and you did not remarry or enter into another registered domestic partnership in 2025"), so "if both" cannot apply there either. Line 9 (senior): Form 540 line 9 "Senior: If you (or your spouse/RDP) are 65 or older, enter 1; if both are 65 or older, enter 2." Booklet p. 12, Line 9: "If you were 65 years of age or older by December 31, 2025*, you should claim an additional exemption credit on line 9. If you are married/or an RDP, each spouse/RDP 65 years of age or older should claim an additional credit." "*If your 65th birthday is on January 1, 2026, you are considered to be age 65 on December 31, 2025." "Do not claim this credit if someone else can claim you as a dependent on their tax return." Only a joint return enters 2: the second count is the spouse/RDP's ("if both"). A single or head-of-household return has no spouse/RDP on it, and a separate return counts the filer alone (booklet p. 5, "Married/RDP Filing Separately": "You cannot claim a personal exemption credit for your spouse/RDP even if your spouse/RDP had no income, is not filing a tax return, and is not claimed as a dependent on another person's tax return."). On a qualifying surviving spouse/RDP return the spouse/RDP died in an earlier year (p. 5: "Your spouse/RDP died in 2023 or 2024 and you did not remarry or enter into another registered domestic partnership in 2025"), so "if both" cannot apply there either. Line 10 (dependent): Form 540 line 10 "Dependents: Do not include yourself or your spouse/RDP." Booklet p. 12, Line 10: "To claim an exemption credit for each of your dependents, you must write each dependent's first and last name, SSN or ITIN, and relationship to you in the space provided."
